issues.description: The template file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java declares a public class named AnimalFarm and contains duplicated/incorrect package declarations and malformed content, while the problem statement and solution expect a class named Farm (matching the filename). This structural mismatch (class name/file name mismatch and malformed template) will prevent students from compiling and from following the UML/specification which requires a Farm class with the specified methods/attributes.
issues.suggestedFix: Restore src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java to declare public class Farm (matching the filename) and remove the duplicated/incorrect package declaration and malformed duplicate class content. Ensure Farm has the intended private List<Animal> animals field, a no-argument constructor initializing an ArrayList, getters/setters, addAnimal, feedAllAnimals, singFarmSong, and a private singFarmSongVerse(Animal) helper as specified in the problem statement so the template compiles and aligns with the UML/spec.

issues.description: The problem statement and the reference solution define a class named 'Farm', but the template starter file declares the class as 'AnimalFarm'. This discrepancy means students looking for the required Farm class in the template will not find the expected identifier, breaking the direct mapping from the exercise description to the starter code and causing unnecessary confusion about which class to implement or extend.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the class declared in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java from 'AnimalFarm' to 'Farm' (and update the file if necessary) so the template uses the same identifier as the problem statement and the solution. Ensure the public class name matches the file name 'Farm.java'.
